intimation

/in-tuh-MAY-shun/ - the stress falls on MAY · noun

Hear It

What It Means

Intimation means an indirect hint or suggestion.

A ring around the moon was the crew's only intimation of the gale still a day out.

Example

No one told Teo his sister was engaged. The intimations piled up anyway: a ring-sized box in the recycling, a sudden interest in June weekends, their mother humming the same march she had hummed before his own wedding. When the announcement finally came at Sunday dinner, Teo had already drafted his speech.

Intimation is the exact word for those clues, because an intimation is an indirect hint or suggestion — something shown at the edge of your eye rather than said to your face. An announcement declares; an intimation lets you notice. And it must come from outside: a dread with no sign behind it at all is a premonition, a word waiting in this unit's reference list.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

inkling: An inkling is the faint idea that forms inside you — a first vague sense that something is coming. An intimation is the outward signal that plants that idea: a small sign out in the world rather than a feeling in your head. No sign, no intimation.

whisper: A whisper is a hint passed quietly from person to person — someone chooses to pass it along, however softly. An intimation need not come from anyone on purpose: a look, a habit, a light left on can give one off without a word being spoken.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

proclamation: the thing said outright, for all to hear

announcement: news delivered plainly

Where it sits · how openly the message is stated

intimation → hint → declaration

hint vs. intimation: A hint goes further than an intimation — a hint wants to be caught; an intimation barely troubles the surface, and missing it is no failure.

declaration vs. intimation: A declaration goes much further than an intimation — nothing indirect is left in it; the thing is simply said, in full, on the record.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — intim: innermost (Latin intimus)

Suffix — -ation: the act of

Put it together: Intim- (innermost) + -ation (the act of) = the act of bringing something out from the innermost layer. Latin intimare meant to make known what was inside; an intimation still only cracks the door — the inner thing shows one edge, no more.

Use the root in a new word: intimate: Your intimate friends are the ones admitted nearest your innermost self — the same intim- that lets an intimation slip out from under the surface.

Strength Check

Word Choice

formal / literary

Intimation is for hints so oblique they barely exist — the first intimations of trouble. A hint expects to be caught; an intimation can be missed without blame. It needs an outward sign, however small; a certainty that rises inside you with no sign at all is a premonition, which waits in this unit's reference list.
